narrative.overview: LinuxMatch reads like a well-labelled specimen drawer: a working tool whose visual language comes from field guides, catalogue plates and annotation marks rather than from the terminal or the marketing landing page. The page stays calm and paper-like; meaning is carried by hairline rules, alignment and tabular metadata, not by ornament. Lime is annotation ink, used only for actions and active states.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and graphite grounds with identical role structure
Hairline rules, tabular metadata and generous margins
One lime accent reserved for action and selection

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Lime marks a decision or an action. If it decorates a static surface, remove it.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: Show distro screenshots whole and caption them; never crop them into a false comparison.

dos: Do use verified catalogue data and local assets.
Do keep body text in Public Sans and measurements in Geist Mono.
Do preserve focus visibility and reduced-motion behavior.
donts: Don't use gradients, neon glow, emoji icons or hard offset shadows.
Don't use decorative kickers or rounded-card filler.
